title.en: Finding the LCM through prime factorisation

text.en:
Two bells ring every 12 and 18 minutes and the teacher asked when they ring together.
"Use prime factors," said Meena.

Write each number as a product of primes: 12 is 2 x 2 x 3 and 18 is 2 x 3 x 3. For the LCM take each prime to its highest power: 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 is 36.
For the HCF take each common prime to its lowest power: 2 x 3 is 6.
A useful property: HCF times LCM of two numbers equals their product. 6 x 36 = 216 = 12 x 18.
Write each number as a product of primes: 12 is 2 x 2 x 3 and 18 is 2 x 3 x 3.
For the LCM take each prime to its highest power: 2 x 2 x 3 x 3 is 36.
For the HCF take each common prime to its lowest power: 2 x 3 is 6.
A useful property: HCF times LCM of two numbers equals their product.

problem.en: Find the LCM of 12 and 18 using primes.

text.en: LCM is 2 x 2 x 3 x 3, which is 36.

prompt.en: A friend says HCF x LCM is different from the product of the numbers. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: For two numbers they are equal.

points.en: HCF x LCM = product of two numbers.
